## Summary

Implements `/task --ci-cd <repository>` as the issue-creation-only fallback for `/fix --ci-cd` (issue #2121).

The command now:

1. accepts both ASCII `--ci-cd` and the reported typographic `—ci-cd` spelling;
2. collects the target repository's languages, default-branch commit, and CI/CD runs;
3. creates the same typed CI/CD remediation issue as `/fix --ci-cd`;
4. returns the full created-issue URL without starting `/fix` or `/solve`; and
5. tells the user to reply with `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge` to continue normally.

## Root cause

Telegram's shared argument parser already normalized the reported em dash and tokenized the option before the repository URL. The `/task` handler, however, only distinguished ordinary issue creation from split mode. It therefore sent the complete option-and-URL line to the free-form issue parser, which could not find the repository in its expected standalone form and returned “Missing GitHub repository URL.”

The network-backed CI/CD collector also lived inside executable `fix.mjs`, preventing `/task` from reusing only the issue-creation stage without duplication or spawning the full workflow.

## Implementation

- Extract `prepareCiCdIssue()` and `createCiCdIssue()` into a shared service used by both `/fix` and `/task`.
- Add a dedicated `/task --ci-cd` handler path before ordinary issue parsing.
- Preserve the existing title/body builders, commit-to-branch run fallback, Bug type, and `bug` label fallback.
- Reject missing repositories and issue/PR URLs; reject combining `--ci-cd` with split mode.
- Document the fallback in all four maintained README/help locales.
- Add a minor changeset.
- Add the requested deep case study and machine-readable evidence/source catalogs under `docs/case-studies/issue-2121/`.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Before this change:

```text
/task —ci-cd https://github.com/link-assistant/agent
→ Missing GitHub repository URL
```

The regression test now sends that exact command shape through `handleTaskCommand()` and asserts:

- the parsed repository reaches the shared CI/CD issue generator;
- no managed task or `/fix` execution starts;
- the created issue URL is returned; and
- the exact continuation solve flags are shown.

Additional tests cover ASCII parsing, invalid repository inputs, shared GitHub context collection, prompt generation, and typed issue creation.

## Verification

- `npm test` — all 358 default test files passed
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `node tests/docs-validation.mjs`
- `node tests/test-docs-language-sync.mjs`
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- focused task and CI/CD suites: 28/28 each

Closes #2121.
title: /task --ci-cd: create CI/CD remediation issues without /fix (#2121)

body:
## Problem

`/task --ci-cd https://github.com/link-assistant/agent` created
[link-assistant/agent#287](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/287), whose
"Recent CI/CD runs on `main`" table has **20 rows for only 2 workflows** — the same
*JS CI/CD Pipeline* (14 rows) and *Rust CI/CD Pipeline* (6 rows) repeated for commits
spanning 2026-04-25 … 2026-07-30 — and a summary of "CI/CD runs found: 20 (9 not passing)"
that counts months-old failures as current.

## Root cause

`/fix --ci-cd` and `/task --ci-cd` share `prepareCiCdIssue()`. It lists the runs of the
latest default-branch commit; when that commit produced none — verified for `agent`'s
`fd42c4b` ("0.25.4"): `actions/runs?head_sha=fd42c4b…` returns `total_count: 0` — it falls
back to `actions/runs?branch=main`, which returns runs **across many commits**.
`buildRunsSection()` mapped that array 1:1 to table rows, and `summarizeRunFailures()`
counted it raw. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` has no "latest run per workflow"
option, so the collapse has to happen client-side — and nothing did it.

## Fix

- `runWorkflowKey()` — workflow identity: `workflow_id`, then `path`, then `name`; a run
  with no identifying field is never treated as a duplicate.
- `dedupeRunsByWorkflow()` — keeps the most recent run per workflow (`created_at`, then
  `run_attempt`, then `id`), preserving input order. `countDuplicateRuns()` reports how
  many rows it drops.
- `buildRunsSection()` deduplicates and gained `includeCommit`, so the branch-fallback
  table shows which commit each surviving run belongs to.
- `summarizeRunFailures()` / `buildCiCdIssueBody()` count the deduplicated set, so the
  table and the "CI/CD runs found" line always agree.
- The runs query now selects `workflow_id`, `path`, `created_at`, `run_attempt`, and the
  fallback fetches `per_page=100` instead of `20` — after collapsing, a workflow whose last
  run is older than the 20 most recent would otherwise disappear entirely.
- `prepareCiCdIssue()` returns `fetchedRuns`/`duplicateRuns` and logs
  `ℹ️ Collapsed N older CI/CD run(s) …`, which `/fix` prints.

## Reproduction and verification

Regenerating the issue body from the *exact* 20 runs behind agent#287
(`docs/case-studies/issue-2125/data/`) now yields:

```
| Workflow | Status | Conclusion | Commit | Run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JS CI/CD Pipeline | completed | failure | `cff4148` | [run](.../30572373896) |
| Rust CI/CD Pipeline | completed | failure | `7af549d` | [run](.../28688932169) |
```

with `CI/CD runs found: 2 (2 not passing)`. Full "before" payload, the regenerated body and
the analysis are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2125`](docs/case-studies/issue-2125/README.md).

## Tests

`tests/test-fix-ci-cd.mjs` (suite `default`) gains four regression tests, including an
end-to-end `prepareCiCdIssue()` run through a stubbed `gh` that reproduces the release-commit
→ branch-fallback → duplicate-row path and asserts the stale run is gone, the count is not
inflated, and the verbose collapse line is emitted.

Fixes #2125
title: fix(2125): collapse duplicate CI/CD runs in generated issues

body:
## Summary

Implements `/fix --ci-cd <repository>` (issue #1733): a command that **automatically generates and solves a CI/CD remediation issue** for a target repository, from the CLI or from Telegram.

Given a repository, `/fix --ci-cd`:

1. **Detects languages** via the GitHub `/languages` API and selects the matching CI/CD templates, **ordered by detected language** (byte-weighted; JavaScript + TypeScript merge into one template).
2. **Inspects the latest default-branch commit** and lists its CI/CD runs in the issue. Release/tag commits frequently have no runs of their own, so it **falls back to the most recent default-branch runs** (clearly relabelled "Recent CI/CD runs on `<branch>`").
3. **Creates the remediation issue**, reusing the title and description of [web-capture#139](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139) **exactly, minus the parts `--development-log` and `--deep-analysis` already provide**, and linking to `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`.
4. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, forwarding every option `/fix` does not consume itself (e.g. `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`).
5. Supports `--dry-run` (preview the issue) and `--no-solve` (create only).

## How the "exact title and description, minus what the options provide" rule works

The upstream case-study paragraph is **retired and never represented in the generated prompt**. `--development-log` is its sole replacement and collects under `./dev/log/issues/{id}/pulls/{pr}`; no option combination, including `--no-solve` or a partial option set, restores the old folder convention. The remaining conditional paragraphs carry `providedBy`, the `/solve` option that injects their equivalent instruction:

| Paragraph | `providedBy` | Dropped when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compile data / retired case study | — | always excluded; replaced by `--development-log` |
| Provide debug output | `--deep-analysis` | `--deep-analysis` is passed |
| Report upstream template issues | `--deep-analysis` | `--deep-analysis` is passed |
| Compare full file tree / best-practices link / keep-working | — | never |

The behavior is derived from reading `buildDeepAnalysisPrompt` and `buildDevelopmentLogPrompt` rather than guessed. Two details matter:

- **The issue is created as type `Bug`** (with the `bug` label). `buildDeepAnalysisPrompt` only emits the root-cause / debug-output / report-upstream instructions for Bug-typed issues, so the Bug type is what makes dropping those paragraphs valid. Issue types are org-scoped and labels are repo-scoped, so both are best-effort: creation retries without the metadata rather than aborting.
- **There is no legacy fallback.** Review feedback clarified that the upstream case-study paragraph conflicts with `--development-log`; it was removed as a constant and paragraph entry, rather than merely hidden by the default option set. Regression tests cover default, no-options, development-log-only, and deep-analysis-only prompt construction.

## Requirements coverage (issue #1733)

| Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- |
| New `/fix --ci-cd` command | ✅ `src/fix.mjs` + `package.json` bin |
| Check latest default-branch commit + list its CI/CD runs | ✅ with branch fallback |
| Use web-capture#139 title **exactly** (as re-titled upstream) | ✅ `CI_CD_ISSUE_TITLE`, pinned by a test |
| Use the description exactly, **omitting** parts `--development-log`/`--deep-analysis` provide | ✅ retired paragraph structurally absent; deep-analysis paragraphs use `providedBy` filtering |
| Template links sorted by detected languages | ✅ `mapLanguagesToTemplates` |
| Detect languages used in the repository | ✅ `gh api .../languages` |
| Behave like `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge` | ✅ `buildSolveArgs` (each flag deduped) |
| Pass through `--tool`/`--model`/`--think` (and every other non-fix option) | ✅ `partitionFixArgs` |
| Link to `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` in the issue | ✅ |
| `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` updated in all languages (en/zh/hi/ru) | ✅ |
| Add PHP template to the list | ✅ `link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |
| Compile data + deep case study to `docs/case-studies/issue-1733/` | ✅ re-done against the updated description |
| Apply the change everywhere it belongs (whole-repo scope, per review) | ✅ Telegram `/fix`, `--fix`/`TELEGRAM_FIX`, help text + docs in 4 locales |

## Architecture

- **`src/fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs`** — pure, network-free core (template mapping, language normalization, tagged-paragraph issue-body building, arg partitioning). Deliberately avoids importing `github.lib.mjs` (whose transitive chain performs a top-level network fetch) so unit tests run fast and offline.
- **`src/fix.mjs`** — thin CLI that talks to `gh`, creates the issue via the existing `/task` `createTaskIssue` helper, and spawns `solve.mjs`.
- **`src/telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`** — the in-chat `/fix` handler, mirroring `telegram-task-command.lib.mjs`: implies `--ci-cd`, normalizes `owner/repo` to a full URL, forwards the chat locale as `--language`, validates model/isolation, and ignores forwarded/replied commands (#1922). Toggle with `--no-fix` / `TELEGRAM_FIX=false`.
- **`src/telegram.config.lib.mjs`** — the bot's yargs option surface, extracted from `telegram-bot.mjs` (adding `--fix` pushed it past the repo's 1500-line `max-lines` cap). Mirrors the existing `solve.config.lib.mjs` / `hive.config.lib.mjs` / `task.config.lib.mjs` pattern, and makes the option surface testable without starting a bot.

## Documentation

- `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` (+ `.zh`, `.hi`, `.ru`): PHP template rows (templates, formatting/PHP CS Fixer, static analysis/PHPStan, changeset/changelog.d) and a new **Automatic CI/CD Remediation** section with the language → template mapping.
- `README.md` (+ `.zh`, `.hi`, `.ru`): new `/fix - Auto-Remediate CI/CD` command section.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (+ 3 locales): the `TELEGRAM_FIX` toggle.
- `src/locales/{en,hi,ru,zh}.lino`: `/fix` help text.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-1733/`: deep analysis (requirements R1–R25, solution plans, reused-components map), captured data (`data/`), and `research-sources.json`.

## Tests

- `tests/test-fix-ci-cd.mjs` — **27 tests.** PHP template, repo parsing, language normalization/sorting, JS+TS merge, unmatched languages, template-section priority + fallback, run summarization, run-table rendering, issue title/body sections + sorting, branch-fallback heading, **the paragraph-omission matrix plus a structural no-fallback assertion**, arg partitioning, and solve-arg assembly.
- `tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs` — **22 tests.** Command recognition, `--ci-cd` implied and not duplicated, option preservation, shorthand normalization, missing repo, non-GitHub URL rejection, spawn args/tool/isolation/urlContext, locale forwarding, invalid isolation/model, forwarded-or-reply ignored, disabled instance, stopped chat, non-group, unauthorized topic, old message, and regex registration.
- `tests/test-telegram-config.mjs` — **6 tests.** Every command enabled by default, `--no-fix`, `TELEGRAM_FIX=false`/`true`, `--fix` overriding the env, strict-mode rejection, isolation default.

All three are in the default suite. `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` are clean.

## How to reproduce / try

```bash
# Preview without creating anything:
fix link-assistant/hive-mind --ci-cd --dry-run

# Create the issue but do not start /solve:
fix link-assistant/hive-mind --ci-cd --no-solve

# Full flow, forwarding solve options:
fix link-assistant/hive-mind --ci-cd --tool codex --model gpt-5.5 --think max
```

From Telegram (`--ci-cd` is implied):

```
/fix https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind --model sonnet
```

Closes #1733.
title: /fix --ci-cd: auto-generate and solve CI/CD remediation issues (#1733)

body:
## Problem

A `fix` run ended with a Telegram notification saying only `Work session failed (exit code: 1)`. Its wrapper log ([raw logs](https://github.com/konard/private-logs/tree/main/log-tmp-start-command-logs-isolation-docker-2757eeb3-68e6-43bb-8a6a-20c55dfd2958)) is **286,452,210 bytes / 1,354,860 lines** and ends in a V8 heap abort:

```text
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
❌ Error: solve exited with code null
Reason: exitCode=1 oomKilled=false
```

The log was large because hive-mind wrote its own output into it, repeatedly. `getPullRequestChangeStats()` ran `gh pr diff` with `command-stream`'s default `mirror: true`, so the whole diff was echoed to stdout, copied into the session log by the stdio interceptor (#1549), published by `--attach-logs` and committed into the branch by `--development-log` — so the *next* `gh pr diff` contained the previous log. The development-log slice committed per iteration went 2.7 MB → 38 MB → 80 MB → 199 MB.

## How to reproduce

Run `solve`/`fix` with `--attach-logs --development-log` on a pull request whose branch already carries a committed session log: each iteration mirrors the whole diff into the log, and the log is committed again. `docs/case-studies/issue-2135/scripts/measure-session-log.mjs <log>` reproduces every number quoted in the case study from the raw log.

## Root causes and fixes

| # | Root cause | Fix |
| - | ---------- | --- |
| RC1 | `gh pr diff` probed with default mirroring, so the diff entered the session log | `src/pull-request-changes.lib.mjs` probes quietly and warns past 8 MB |
| RC2 | The same loud-probe pattern in 12 other modules; `contributing-guidelines` also called `.raw()` on the retry-wrapped `$`, a `TypeError` that silently disabled guideline detection | quiet-probe sweep over 13 modules; `.raw()` removed |
| RC3 | `measureDiff` kept several whole-diff copies plus one match array entry per added line | single streaming pass, returning `diffBytes` |
| RC4 | V8 `abort()` → `SIGABRT` → `code === null`; `hive` computed `code \|\| 0`, recording an OOM-killed worker as a **success** | new `src/child-exit.lib.mjs`, used by all seven spawners |
| RC5 | The log grew 19 MB → 199 MB without a word | new `src/log-growth.lib.mjs`: warnings at 64 MB / 256 MB / 1 GB |
| RC6 | A failed development-log publication left its copies untracked; watch mode read them as the AI's uncommitted work and restarted the session with instructions to commit them | `discardUnpublishedDevelopmentLog()` cleans up on every publication failure path |

## Tests

`tests/test-issue-2135-log-explosion.mjs` — 32 tests in the `default` suite:

- the diff probe is called with `mirror: false, capture: true` and prints nothing (verified with a `$` double that records its options);
- a synthetic 9 MB diff is measured correctly, reports `diffBytes` and produces a warning naming the usual cause;
- source sweeps assert all 13 probes stay quiet, that `contributing-guidelines` never calls `.raw()`, and that all 7 spawner modules describe how their child ended instead of interpolating a null code;
- `attachChildExitHandlers` maps `close(null, 'SIGABRT')` to exit 1 with one error log, and passes ordinary exits through unchanged;
- the growth tracker warns once per threshold and resets with the log file;
- a development-log publication that cannot stage, inspect or commit removes what it wrote, while a successful one keeps its artifacts.

Full `default` suite and `npm run lint` / `npm run format:check` pass locally.

## Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-2135/` holds the deep analysis required by the issue: the requirement inventory, the line-numbered timeline (16:52:17 → 18:26:42), the amplification table, RC1–RC6, the solution plan, prior art (`command-stream` mirror/capture, Node `maxBuffer`, `execa`, `gh pr diff --name-only`, log rotation, `--max-old-space-size` — and why the last two were rejected), and bounded raw excerpts with SHA-256 checksums. The 286 MB log itself is deliberately not committed; the measuring script regenerates its metrics.

The issue also asks whether this belongs in another project: it does not. Every link in the chain is hive-mind's own code.

Fixes #2135
title: fix(2135): stop the session log from swallowing the pull request diff

body:
## Summary

Fixes #2085.

`/fix --ci-cd` **does** call the real `/solve` in a real working session — this
is proven by the captured solve-session metadata of the run cited in the issue,
PR #2083, whose `rawCommand` is a genuine `node .../src/solve.mjs …` invocation.
The actual defect is narrower: the Telegram bot's **operator solve overrides**
(`TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES`, e.g. `--attach-logs`) were merged into `/solve` and
`/hive` but **never into `/fix`**. So the solve launched by `/fix` ran without
the operator's configured defaults — exactly the "`--attach-logs` were not
applied" symptom.

Per #1733, `/fix` should behave as a straightforward combination of `/task` +
`/solve`. This PR makes `/fix` reuse the **identical** override mechanism
`/solve` already uses — no new/fancy machinery.

## Root cause

`mergeArgsWithOverrides()` lived inside `telegram-bot.mjs` and was only applied
by the `/solve` and `/hive` handlers. The `/fix` handler
(`telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`) never received `solveOverrides`, so the
overrides were absent from the args forwarded to `solve.mjs`. The override must
be baked into the **arguments** (not read from env by `fix.mjs`) because Docker
isolation only forwards explicitly-listed `-e` env vars into the container, so a
Docker `/fix` session would never see `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES`.

## Changes

- **`src/args-overrides.lib.mjs`** (new): shared `mergeArgsWithOverrides`
  extracted from `telegram-bot.mjs` (adds `Array.isArray` null-safety) so
  `/solve`, `/hive` and `/fix` share one implementation without a circular
  import on the bot entry point.
- **`src/telegram-bot.mjs`**: import the shared helper; pass `solveOverrides`
  into `registerFixCommand`.
- **`src/telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`**: merge `solveOverrides` into the fix
  args (overrides win, appended last for yargs' last-wins parsing), honor an
  optional `--isolation` override from the overrides, validate the model on the
  merged args, and surface a `🔒 Solve overrides: …` line in the work-session
  info block.
- **Tests**: `tests/test-args-overrides.mjs` (new unit tests for the real
  helper) and new `/fix` override cases in `tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs`.
- **Case study**: `docs/case-studies/issue-2085/` — timeline, requirements,
  root-cause analysis, solution, codebase audit, and existing-components review,
  with primary evidence (`data/pr-2083-solve-metadata.json`).
- **Changeset**: patch bump.

## How to reproduce (before the fix)

1. Run the Telegram bot with `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES="(\n  --attach-logs\n)"`.
2. Trigger `/fix <repo>`; it generates the CI/CD issue and starts `/solve`.
3. Inspect the started solve's `rawCommand` (session `metadata.json`): it lacks
   `--attach-logs` (see PR #2083's captured metadata). After this fix, the
   override is present.

## Verification

- `tests/test-args-overrides.mjs` — 8/8 pass.
- `tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs` — 28/28 pass (7 new override cases).
- `tests/test-issue-1228-options-deduplication.mjs` — 19/19 pass (no regression
  in existing override behaviour).
title: fix(2085): apply solve overrides to the /solve started by /fix

body:
## Problem

Hive Mind commands kept dying at startup while loading `command-stream`, in two
alternating shapes. From the two logs attached to the issue — the *same* command,
`fix https://github.com/link-assistant/agent --ci-cd --attach-logs --verbose`, one
image apart:

```text
# 2.11.1
npm error ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '.../command-stream-v-latest/examples'
Failed to install command-stream@latest globally into '...' after 3 attempts.
```

```text
# 2.10.2
Failed to import module from '.../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.mjs?use-m-retry=1'.
Caused by: Cannot find module '.../command-stream-v-latest/src/shell-parser.mjs'
```

The missing file changed every run (`shell-parser.mjs`, `terminal-capture.mjs`,
`$.trace.mjs`), and `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` shows all of
them are published — so this was never a bad release.

## Root cause

`use()` runs one `npm install -g <alias>@npm:<package>@<version>` per call and has
**no in-flight deduplication**. Node evaluates sibling top-level-await subgraphs
concurrently ([proved locally](experiments/issue-2113/prove-top-level-await-concurrency.mjs):
peak concurrency 3 of 3), and 38 modules under `src/` load `command-stream` through
`use()`, 31 of them at top level — so a cold container running `fix` launches **six
simultaneous global installs of one directory**. npm does not lock the global prefix,
so those installs delete and re-extract each other's trees: the loser gets `ENOTEMPTY`,
and whoever reads a half-extracted tree gets `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for whichever file
was not written yet.

use-m's own recovery amplifies it: `installPackage()` runs
`removePackageAlias(packagePath, 'incomplete')` after *every* failed attempt, so the
loser recursively deletes the tree the winner just installed successfully — which is
exactly how a process that saw no error at all ends up with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

**Retrying cannot help, because every retry re-enters the same race** — visible verbatim
in the 2.11.1 log, where all three of use-m's attempts fail on the same path within nine
seconds.

Reproduced three ways, all recorded under
[`docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw):

| Reproduction | Result |
| --- | --- |
| npm alone, 24 concurrent installs of one alias | 22/24 fail, alias gone afterwards |
| npm alone, 5 concurrent installs of *different* packages (control) | 0/5 fail |
| stock use-m 8.14.4 from the CDN, 8 concurrent `use('command-stream')` | 2/8 fail |
| end to end, 24 concurrent loads, unguarded | **24/24 fail in 54.8 s** |
| end to end, 24 concurrent loads, guarded | **0/24 in 3.3 s** |

The control is what narrows the fix to a **per-alias** lock rather than a global install
lock that would needlessly serialise unrelated dependencies.

### Why the "two commands" workaround appeared to work

The issue reports that splitting the work into `/task --ci-cd` + `/claude <issue>` never
fails. That is consistent with the race, not against it:
[`measure-entrypoint-fanout.mjs`](experiments/issue-2113/measure-entrypoint-fanout.mjs)
walks each binary's import graph and counts reachable modules that top-level-await a
`command-stream` load:

```text
binary              modules   cold burst (static)   reachable (incl. dynamic)
task                93        6                     8
fix                 95        6                     8
review              90        5                     9
solve               156       1                     25
```

`/task --ci-cd` never spawns anything — `src/telegram-task-command.lib.mjs:177` calls
`createCiCdIssueFn()` in the already-warm bot process, so it installs nothing — and
`/claude <issue>` spawns `solve`, whose cold burst is exactly one loader. The workaround
reduced exposure; it did not remove it.

## Fix

`src/use-m-single-flight.lib.mjs` (new, Node built-ins only) wraps `use()` inside
`ensureUseM()`, so all 72 files that bootstrap through it inherit three guards with no
call-site changes:

1. **Per-specifier single flight** — a `Map` from specifier to the in-flight promise,
   evicted on rejection so failures stay retryable. Collapses the whole cold wave into
   one install.
2. **In-process per-alias mutex** — a promise chain keyed by the *alias*
   (`command-stream-v-latest`), so `use('command-stream')` and
   `use('command-stream/foo')` serialise while unrelated packages still install in
   parallel.
3. **Cross-process advisory lock** — atomic `mkdir` on `<alias>.lock`, `utimes`
   heartbeat, stale-steal and timeout, so a bot, a container and a CI step sharing one
   npm prefix cannot collide either. Degrades to in-process-only if the lock root is
   unusable; relocatable with `HIVE_MIND_USE_M_LOCK_DIR`. Built-ins (`use('fs')`) are
   deduplicated but never take the lock.

`useWithRetry()` is kept underneath as recovery for corruption that already exists — the
new layer is prevention, which retries could not provide.

The guard deliberately has no dependencies: it is the thing that makes loading
dependencies safe, so it cannot itself require `proper-lockfile` or `p-memoize`. Their
designs are followed (`mkdir` strategy, `mtime` staleness; `stale: 10000`/`update: stale/2`
informed `DEFAULT_STALE_MS = 15000`/`DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS = 1000`), documented in
[`research.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/research.md).

## Diagnostics

Both attached logs were produced **with `--verbose`** and contained no loader output at
all, which is why the first analysis had to work backwards from a stack trace. Loader
tracing now activates on `--verbose` as well as `HIVE_MIND_USE_M_DEBUG=1`:

```text
[use-m] use('command-stream') loading (alias command-stream-v-latest)
[use-m] use('command-stream') joined an in-flight load (alias command-stream-v-latest)
[use-m] use('command-stream') loaded in 2841ms
```

## Upstream

Reported to use-m as
[link-foundation/use-m#70](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/70) with a
standalone reproduction (no Hive Mind code), the downstream workaround, and a suggested
patch: in-flight dedup, a cross-process install lock, not deleting the alias after a
failed attempt without holding that lock, and verifying after install instead of before.
Preserved in
[`upstream-use-m-concurrency-report.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/upstream-use-m-concurrency-report.md).

**Fixed upstream and released as `use-m@8.15.0`** (2026-07-31T20:23:48Z), which adopts
the suggested cross-process lock: `.use-m/<alias>.lock` taken with atomic `mkdir` plus an
`utimes` heartbeat and stale-steal, and a `.use-m/<alias>.installed.json` marker written
only after `npm install` returns, which `isPackageInstalled()` now requires — closing the
check-then-act window that let a caller import a half-extracted tree. Re-verified here
with the same standalone reproduction, 24 concurrent `use('command-stream')` calls on a
cold prefix:

| use-m | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 8.14.4 | 22/24 fail in 58.3 s ([log](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw/experiment-upstream-use-m-8.14.4-control.log)) |
| 8.15.0 | **0/24 in 3.5 s** ([log](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw/experiment-upstream-use-m-8.15.0-fixed.log)) |

The pinned CDN bootstrap fallback therefore moves from 8.14.4 to 8.15.0 (and the test's
version floor with it). The downstream guard is kept rather than removed: it is what still
holds when the CDN serves an older bundle, and its per-specifier single flight collapses
the cold wave into *one* `npm install` instead of serialising several, which the upstream
lock alone does not do.

Earlier rounds of this issue produced
[#66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) → `use-m@8.14.3` and
[#68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68) → `use-m@8.14.4`, both fixed and
released. No use-m problem found in this issue is unreported. `command-stream` was audited
and cleared — no report filed.

## Tests

- `tests/test-use-m-single-flight-2113.mjs` — 20 tests: dedup, alias serialisation,
  parallelism across aliases, failure eviction, lock acquire/wait/steal/timeout/degrade,
  idempotent wrapping, composition with the retry wrapper, and that `ensureUseM()`
  installs the guard. Includes an **unguarded control** asserting that 35 of 36 concurrent
  loads break without it.
- Opt-in reproductions under `experiments/issue-2113/` (network + npm).

```bash
node tests/test-use-m-single-flight-2113.mjs   # 20/20
npm run lint                                    # clean
npm test
```

## Case study

[`docs/case-studies/issue-2113/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2113) holds every supplied log,
the workaround screenshot, the package/release audit, the recorded output of every
experiment, plus `timeline.md`, `requirements.md` (R1–R16, each mapped to evidence),
`analysis.md` and `research.md`.

Fixes #2113
title: fix(2113): dedupe and lock concurrent use-m installs

body:
## Summary

Fixes #1952. Two distinct bugs surfaced by [xlabtg/teleton-agent PR #670](https://github.com/xlabtg/teleton-agent/pull/670):

1. **Timeout-cancelled CI was misclassified as "requires review".** A job that hits its `timeout-minutes` limit surfaces as a **check-run** with conclusion `cancelled`, but the **parent workflow run** concludes `failure`. `getDetailedCIStatus` inspects check-runs only, so the auto-merge loop saw the lone `cancelled` check, posted a **"Cancelled CI/CD Requires Review"** comment, and stopped — even though the workflow run had failed and *other jobs in it had also failed*.
2. **The session finished with no log attached despite `--attach-logs`.** Every log-attachment path in `solve.mjs` is conditional, and the stop-for-human-review exits can `return` before any iteration uploads a log.

## Root cause

GitHub reports a timed-out job at two levels with different conclusions:

| Inspect… | Timeout looks like… | Manual cancel looks like… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| check-runs only (old behaviour) | `cancelled` ❌ | `cancelled` |
| workflow runs (the fix) | `failure` ✅ | `cancelled` |

The real teleton run `27821270533` concluded `failure` with jobs `Build (Runtime) (22)`, `Deploy artifacts`, `OpenAPI` all **failed** plus `Build (Runtime) (20)` **cancelled** (timeout) — yet the tool stopped for review. Full evidence and analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-1952/`](./docs/case-studies/issue-1952/README.md).

## Changes

### R1 + R2 — classify cancelled CI by workflow-run conclusions
- New pure helper `classifyCancelledCIByWorkflowRuns` + `FAILURE_LIKE_WORKFLOW_RUN_CONCLUSIONS` (`failure`, `timed_out`, `startup_failure`) in `src/cancelled-ci-rerun.lib.mjs`.
- `getMergeBlockers` (`src/solve.auto-merge-helpers.lib.mjs`) cancelled branch now fetches the workflow runs for the SHA and classifies:
  - **pending** (any run not yet terminal) → `ci_pending` → keep waiting until *all* checks are terminal (R2).
  - **failure** (any completed failure-like run) → `ci_failure` → restart the AI to fix it (R1; R2 coexisting failures).
  - **cancelled** → original re-triggerable flow (genuine manual cancellation).
- `src/solve.auto-merge.lib.mjs`: the "Cancelled CI/CD Requires Review" stop path is skipped when a `ci_failure` blocker coexists.
- `src/github-merge-ci.lib.mjs`: `startup_failure` now counts as a failing run (applied codebase-wide, R7).

### R3 — guarantee a log is always attached
- `attachLogToGitHub` (`src/github.lib.mjs`) sets `global.logAttachedToGitHub = true` on **every** successful upload (both upload branches).
- New `attachFinalLogIfMissing` (`src/attach-logs-guarantee.lib.mjs`) runs as the last step of `solve.mjs`: attaches the cumulative session log when `--attach-logs` is on, a PR exists, and nothing attached yet, then reconciles `logsAttached` so `endWorkSession` does not double-post.

### R4/R5/R6
- `docs/case-studies/issue-1952/` — downloaded evidence + deep analysis (timeline, requirements R1–R8, root causes, existing-component review). Verbose logging added in the cancelled branch (off by default). No third-party repo bug to report — the behaviour was entirely in hive-mind's own logic; GitHub Actions behaves as documented.

## How to reproduce (before the fix)
A PR whose CI workflow run concludes `failure` while one of its jobs is `cancelled` by `timeout-minutes`: the old code posted "Cancelled CI/CD Requires Review" and stopped instead of restarting the AI, and finished the session with no attached log.

## Tests
- `tests/test-cancelled-timeout-fail-1952.mjs` — 13 tests. Reproduces the teleton case (workflow-run `failure` + cancelled check → `failure`) and covers `timed_out`/`startup_failure`/manual-cancel/`stale`/mixed/in-progress/queued/empty + wiring.
- `tests/test-attach-logs-safety-net-1952.mjs` — 9 tests. Global flag set only on real uploads; `attachFinalLogIfMissing` disabled / no-PR / already-attached / fires-as-last-resort; solve.mjs wiring.

Both pass locally; the changeset bumps `@link-assistant/hive-mind` (patch).
title: fix(auto-merge): treat timeout-cancelled CI as failure; always attach logs (#1952)

Fixes #2025.

## Summary

- Lazy-load `command-stream`/`use-m` in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs` so importing pure helper exports no longer performs a network fetch.
- Add a regression test that stubs `globalThis.fetch`, imports the isolation runner, and asserts the import made zero fetch calls.
- Rename stale CI step labels from `Use Node.js 20.x` to `Use Node.js 24.x` where the workflow already used Node 24.
- Update `azure/setup-helm` from `v4` to `v5`; upstream `v5` uses `node24`, removing the fresh PR warning about Node 20 action runtimes being forced onto Node 24.
- Preserve the failed-run logs, metadata, local check logs, and CI/CD template snapshots under `docs/case-studies/issue-2025/`.

## Root Cause

Run `29020837748` failed in `test-suites` at `[97/309] tests/test-isolation-runner.mjs` with `TypeError: fetch failed` and Cloudflare `ETIMEDOUT`/IPv6 `ENETUNREACH` errors. The test only needed pure helpers, but `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs` initialized `use-m` and loaded `command-stream` at module top level, so import-time module evaluation depended on a live external CDN fetch.

That made the CI failure a false negative caused by an external network timeout rather than an isolation-runner behavior regression.

## Template Comparison

Downloaded and compared the JavaScript, Rust, Python, and C# AI-driven development pipeline template trees and release workflows. The JavaScript template is the closest match and uses Node 24 plus an `npm test` gate, but none of the templates contain this repository's local `isolation-runner.lib.mjs` import-time dependency. No upstream template issue was filed.

## Verification

- `node tests/test-isolation-runner.mjs`
- `node --check src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`
- `node --check tests/test-isolation-runner.mjs`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`
- `git diff --cached --check`
- `npm test` completed locally with `All 309 selected test file(s) passed.`
- After the Helm action update: `npm run format:check` and `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- GitHub Actions `Checks and release` run `29033108807` completed successfully on commit `b0e58626020146a1668ea1dfa8a1c44b6a93da77`: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/29033108807

Local note: this workspace has Node `v20.20.2`, while package metadata and CI require Node `>=24.0.0`; the saved install log includes the expected engine warnings. GitHub Actions is the authoritative Node 24 verification.
title: Fix CI false negative from isolation runner import-time fetch
